symptom: The devlab renderer can produce frames through a second capture driver that skips the product headless capture lifecycle and its character GLB readiness wait.
direct_cause: src/devlab/directorRender.tsx owns a CaptureDriver that duplicates seek, settle, camera selection, and capture calls instead of mounting DirectorHeadlessCapture.
class_root: Frame capture has no single shared product boundary for scene readiness, camera selection, and capture metadata.
affected_population: Product staging and camera move headless captures
entry_points: DirectorHeadlessCapture mounted by the devlab director renderer
internal_only_reason: The invariant is application-owned: all callers must mount the product capture component and receive its readiness and readback contract.
invariants: Every headless capture waits for visible characterMount objects; callers that opt into action readiness also wait until referenced pose clips are ready.
Every captured frame is produced by SceneRegistry.captureFrame and carries the camera id and actual camera readback when available.
Existing callers that omit optional props retain first-camera selection and burned labels.

door_reduction.why_not: The seven read doors are public type/component consumers and must remain: staging and camera-move production callers keep their existing lifecycle, the component owns its own result contract, and the devlab caller is added as a third consumer. They converge on DirectorHeadlessCapture rather than being removed.

generality_proof: The production staging and camera-move callers and the devlab renderer all mount the same DirectorHeadlessCapture component. Optional camera selection, label settings, exact dimensions, and action-readiness waiting are resolved inside its shared CaptureDriver, while CaptureBinder returns the same actual camera and subject readback for every caller.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own character readiness, timeline seek/settle, camera selection, and per-frame result assembly.
Render through the product CaptureBinder and return actual camera and subject world readback.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: StagingCaptureHost already mounts the shared component and receives its frames result.
CameraMoveCaptureHost already mounts the shared component for frameTimes and retains default props.
The devlab renderer now mounts the product component and only adapts its callback to the postMessage protocol.

recurrence.reason: Any future renderer or export caller could duplicate the lifecycle and diverge on asset readiness or capture metadata unless the shared component owns the boundary.
same_class_scan: rg CaptureDriver across src/devlab and director agent paths
Checked StagingCaptureHost, CameraMoveCaptureHost, and src/devlab/directorRender.tsx independently

prevention.invariant: All headless callers use the shared readiness wait, optional action-clip readiness, seek/settle loop, CaptureBinder path, and result metadata.
prevention.failure_mode: A missing camera or null frame returns null to the caller; the devlab adapter reports an explicit error to its parent window.
prevention.strategy: Delete the devlab CaptureDriver and mount DirectorHeadlessCapture with an injected camera selector and label option.

legacy_paths.rationale: The duplicated devlab CaptureDriver is removed in favor of the product component; production callers remain on the shared path.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party dependency controls the capture lifecycle invariant.

migration: No persisted data migration is needed; existing callers omit the new optional props and keep their prior defaults.
residual_risks: The judge harness must compare returned frameReadbacks to sampleDirectorProject; this change only exposes the product readback.
Pose readiness and T-pose rejection remain judge-layer checks.

invariant_owner_layer.why: The product headless component owns character readiness, camera selection, seek/settle, and frame result assembly for staging, camera movement, and devlab callers.
